inline.s: The second side of the impact is
the propagation of Japan’s “Benyuan Dharma Gate,”
which seeks to interfere with and destroy it in spirit and in the direction and path of Buddhist study and practice. The entry of Japanese Buddhism into China has been long-standing;
in the 1930s it served the war of aggression against China.

. The essay The Alarm Bell discloses that at that time in Wuhu, Anhui, “in the middle second street there was a Japanese Buddhist temple, with Japanese-style lanterns hung at the gate, bearing the red characters ‘Higashi Honganji,’ and within lived a Japanese monk and his whole family. The Japanese monk often held a leather drum and beat it as he walked along the streets. It is said that in all the other cities occupied by Japan there were such, and that they served with the army, exclusively performing rites for the dead Japanese.

At that time when Japan invaded China, they called it the ‘holy war’; to kill for the ‘holy war’ was without guilt, and the dead souls passed beyond to the Buddha-land. The glorious names of those who killed many Chinese and had merit could enter the ‘shrine.’ After the War of Resistance ended, the unpopular Japanese Buddhism vanished from mainland China.
Who would have thought that this specter has been resurrected by ‘a group of people
(namely Master Huijing, Master Jingzong, and others)
’ — is not that absurd?
The Shanghai layman Zheng Songying, in the essay Destroying the Heterodox and Revealing the Right, Eliminating the Three Harms published in Taizhou Buddhism, points out: “The Japanese
‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ has recently already been transmitted to China
, and though it seems a school of the Pure Land Dharma, it is entirely contrary to the Buddha’s Dharma, misleads sentient beings, and does great harm,
and is in fact a heretic within the teaching!

It advocates that so long as one hears the name of Amitābha Buddha and can bring forth faith, one has obtained the ‘identity card’ of the Land of Utmost Bliss, and is certain to be reborn there! No more reciting the Buddha’s name and practicing; no matter how one dies, and without the deathbed assistance of recitation, one is certain to be reborn!” “The ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ requires only a single ‘faith’ and no ‘practice’ at all, relying on other-power alone and not self-power — is this still Buddhism?” In fact, in the late Qing and early Republican era, the layman Yang Renshan, through the Japanese Buddhist scholar Nanjō Bun’yū, imported a great many Buddhist scriptures, and with regard to the ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ he subjected it to criticism and rejection. (See the Clarification of the Teaching Compilation in the Continued Canon
the twelfth kind compiled by the layman Yang.) No master of the Pure Land school in China’s modern and contemporary period has ever advocated the ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate.’
More and more evidence shows that
the impact of this undercurrent is by no means accidental or spontaneous,
but organized and planned,
backed both by
huge sums of money as its support,
and possessing channels and bases for
printing books and recording tapes,
and moreover possessing those who
preach and incite — monks, nuns, and laypersons and so on.
. About two years ago,
the Japanese Benyuan Dharma Gate got in touch with temples in Jiangxi; if a large ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ center could be established, it could remit ten million yuan.

. At that time they also had doubts about the ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ claim that only a single ‘faith’ is needed and one may dispense with reciting the Buddha’s name and practicing. But they again thought of using this large fund to build a center and in the future still promote the pure and correct Pure Land school, and wrote to the elder layman Zheng Songying in Shanghai to ask his advice. The elder Zheng’s reply pointed out: “To do so is to set an improper motive-ground, and it should be firmly refused and not accepted.” Only then did they desist.
It is now established that the centers propagating the ‘Benyuan Dharma Gate’ are very many, and those with frequent activity number several.
The essay The Alarm Bell says: “In the past two years, Taiwan’s
Japanese Jōdo Shinshū Benyuan Dharma Gate
has repeatedly mailed books, publicity materials, and so on to the various Buddhist institutions of Anhui, and some Buddhists have already come under its influence.”
There are two young and middle-aged home-leavers who call themselves of Mount Jiuhua, propagating Japanese Buddhism in various cities; one of them, eloquent, is called ‘Master Holy Su (
now renamed Master Jingzong, having run off to take refuge with Master Huijing of Taiwan, who advocates the Benyuan Dharma Gate
),’ and using people’s reverence for the sacred ground of Mount Jiuhua and respect for the monks of Mount Jiuhua, they find connections to help them arrange venues to preach,
pleasing the devout good believers of little experience and the home-leavers who do not keep the precepts.

During the Spring Festival this year, the two monks Holy Su and another, accompanied by a Taiwanese nun, came down from the mountain again to preach. From Xuancheng to Wuhu they gave one day’s preaching and one day’s discussion,
and afterward were called to account by the municipal Chinese People’s Political Consultative Conference and the Religious Affairs Bureau.
, in the first half of the year, this undercurrent again penetrated deep into the southwest, and Chongqing Municipality was most heavily affected. Not only did the Cangtangyan

of Xuancheng, Anhui, and the “Ciyuan Group Bodhi Monastery Gift Center” of Dezhou, Shandong, send in bulk such books as the Amitābha Calling series, but in the summer they also sent a young monk to the Chongqing urban area, very secretively, without revealing the name of his original monastery or his Dharma name, lodging in the home of a layperson and organizing group after group of faithful to hear him advocate the “Benyuan Dharma Gate”; those deluded grew daily, until the lay practitioners who practiced the Pure Land Dharma Gate in Chongqing split into two factions. Some lay practitioners who upheld the Pure Land “two powers” (Buddha-power and self-power) Dharma Gate put many questions to this monk, but his replies were unclear, and he even said angrily: “You will fall into hell! Fall into hell! Fall into hell!”
Judging from the above circumstances, if this undercurrent is let to grow and spread, it will severely corrode, and even destroy, the whole of Buddhism.

(Original editor’s note: The Benyuan Dharma Gate distorts the three Pure Land sutras and one treatise, advocating that there is no need to recite sutras, keep the precepts, bring forth bodhicitta, or practice the bodhisattva’s six perfections and ten thousand practices — this altogether contravenes Buddhist doctrine and the Mahāyāna spirit that transcends the world while being in the world,
and is in reality
an outer path attached to Buddhism
, and it should arouse the high regard and resistance of the whole Buddhist community. It is also hoped that the relevant government departments pay attention

blocks.text: Appendix Two: Guard Against the Harm and the Misleading of the Benyuan Dharma Gate on the Pure Land School

inline.s: [Original editor’s note]

The essay Guarding Against the Harm and the Misleading of the Benyuan Dharma Gate on the Pure Land School, in the magazine Sound of the Dharma, the journal of the Buddhist Association of China, lists many false teachings of the Benyuan Dharma Gate, and finally warns that “if its theory is allowed to circulate in the Buddhist community, it will have a destructive influence on the abiding of the true Dharma.”

blocks.text: 1. A Brief Account of the Origin and Development of the Benyuan Dharma Gate

inline.s: The theory of the Benyuan Dharma Gate originated with the Japanese Master Hōnen, and reached its peak with his disciple Shinran.

As the essay in Sound of the Dharma says, “its basic theory single-mindedly emphasizes other-power, and is in many places at variance with the sutras and treatises.” Yang Renshan, the father of the restoration of Chinese Buddhism, in his Critique of the Selected Collection of Original Vow Recitation says: “I find that this collection is at variance with the sutras’ meaning in quite a number of places,” and in his Critique of the Shinshu Doctrine says: “I find it is at variance with the sutras’ meaning in quite a number of places,”
and he criticized their false teaching as “
concealing the mechanism of the destruction of the Dharma
Master Hōnen’s theory had already deviated from Master Shandao, and the Jōdo Shinshū (Benyuan Dharma Gate) established by his disciple Master Shinran ran even more directly counter to Master Shandao.
Master Shandao’s thought is “even the evil person is reborn, how much more the good person”; but with the Jōdo Shinshū it became the “evil person is the true capacity” of “
even the good person is reborn, how much more the evil person”!
The “even ten recitations” of the eighteenth vow is also construed by the Benyuan Dharma Gate as “so long as one deeply believes in Amitābha’s original vow (the eighteenth vow),
with a single recitation one is reborn in the reward land

, and immediately attains Buddhahood, transcending the nine grades. Therefore there is no need for many recitations; otherwise it is not trusting Amitābha’s original vow, and so recitation is only an act of gratitude!”
(One of the characteristics of the Benyuan Dharma Gate: topsy-turvy teaching.)

For this reason, even Master Hōnen himself rebuked Shinran as “an outer path attached to the Buddha’s Dharma, a confederate of the demon hosts, destroying and extinguishing the Buddha’s Dharma, an outer path beyond the outer paths,” and warned the multitude: “Be careful not to follow that false teaching.”
Yet up to the present day, these false teachings that even Hōnen rebuked
have been inherited by Master Huijing and others, who promote the Benyuan Dharma Gate under the banner of the “Shandao school.”
Master Huijing’s The Essence of Master Shandao says: “One does not know that the purpose of the Contemplation Sutra is to manifest Amitābha’s original vow:
the evil person is the true capacity
The Benyuan Dharma Gate is that the evil person is the true capacity

, other-power faith and practice, rebirth in the reward land. That is, the most evil and lowest person, relying on the most excellent and highest Dharma, is born in the highest and most wonderful land.”
Note:

The Sutra Praised by the Buddha: The Pure Land, which our teacher Śākyamuni Buddha proclaimed with his own golden mouth, and which is praised and received by Amitābha Buddha in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss, says:
“Sentient beings of little root of good are not those who can attain rebirth in the pure Buddhaland of the Land of Utmost Bliss of Amitāyus Buddha.
(Translation: sentient beings with little root of good (the good of the three karmic actions of body, speech, and mind) cannot attain rebirth in the Western Land of Utmost Bliss. See
Annotation on the Sutra Praised by the Buddha: The Pure Land

Yet the Benyuan Dharma Gate loudly advocates the evil-person-is-the-true-capacity doctrine, making Amitābha Buddha’s great vow into a protective umbrella for the evil person. Its slandering of the Buddha and destruction of the Dharma go this far!
In the Contemplation Sutra of Infinite Life, the person of the five heinous offenses and ten evil deeds is not one who is reborn merely by reciting the name,
but rather one who has accomplished the ten consecutive recitations at the moment of death and, extinguishing his offenses, is reborn
(see
Annotation on the Lowest Grade and Lowest Birth Section of the Contemplation Sutra
. Originally, the “lowest grade and lowest birth section” of the Contemplation Sutra is about the grade of the person thus reborn
(the person of the five heinous offenses and ten evil deeds who, having accomplished the ten consecutive recitations at the moment of death and extinguished his offenses, is reborn)
, which is the lowest grade and lowest birth; but the Benyuan Dharma Gate deliberately omits
the key of “ten consecutive recitations at the moment of death”

, exaggerating it into the claim that all persons of the five heinous offenses and ten evil deeds who merely recite the Buddha’s name once are reborn, and even advocating the so-called evil-person-is-the-true-capacity doctrine
(that Amitābha Buddha’s salvation takes the evil person as its true capacity)

Moreover, even those in the sutra who are said to attain rebirth despite the five heinous offenses and ten evil deeds did so because in past lives they deeply planted good roots and once sowed the seed of bodhi. Master Ouyi
says
“The sutra says that those who attain rebirth despite the ten evil deeds and five heinous offenses
must have planted the seed of bodhi in the past.
If there were no seed of bodhi, how could they meet a good friend? Even if they met a good friend who urged them on, how could they at once bring forth faith and vow and recite the great name?”
(The Lingfeng Collected Treatises, General Sermon at the Tianma Monastery of Shepu)
